# Bhaddiya Sutta (Ud 2.10 (PTS Ud 18))

**ID:** Ud 2.10 (PTS Ud 18)
**Section:** Udāna (ud)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Bhaddiya Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0503m.mul1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Bhaddiya Sutta* (Ud 2.10; PTS Ud 18) is the tenth discourse of the second chapter of the *Udāna*. The text recounts an inspired exclamation by the monk Bhaddiya (the son of Lady Kāḷigodhā), a former Sakyan royal who had gone forth into the monastic order alongside Anuruddha and other nobles [Buswell & Lopez 2014; Horner, Cullavagga]. While dwelling in solitude beneath a tree in the forest, Bhaddiya repeatedly exclaims over the bliss of his state [Buswell & Lopez 2014; Horner, Cullavagga]. Overhearing his cries, other monks suspect that he is reminiscing about the lost luxuries and status of his former rulership and report him to the Buddha [Horner, Cullavagga]. When questioned, Bhaddiya clarifies that while he formerly lived in constant dread, suspicion, and anxiety despite being surrounded by heavily armed guards, he now dwells peaceful, fearless, and unburdened in the forest, prompting the Buddha to utter an inspired utterance (*udāna*) celebrating his release [Horner, Cullavagga].
